Reverses the order of the bytes of a number, which converts between the order that the processor uses (little endian) and the order that files and networks often use (big endian). A one byte number is returned as it is. The result has the type of the number. This is a BlitzLLVM extension. It looks at the bits of the number the way its type has them, so the same value counts differently as a `Byte`, an `Int` or a `Long`: a number written in the program is an `Int` (32 bits) unless it is larger, and `Byte`, `UByte`, `Short`, `UShort`, `UInt`, `Long` and `ULong` give the other widths. A real or a text is taken as an `Int`, like the bit operators do.

```blitzbasic
;run
Print Hex(ByteSwap($12345678))
Print ByteSwap(UShort($1234))
Print ByteSwap(ULong(1))
```

```text
78563412
13330
72057594037927936
```
@param value  An integer.
@returns The number with its bytes in the other order.
@gap Not in the originals.
